clue.text: Being put out, rate evil member of the family

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed from its order, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone expelled for an evil rate of something is still part of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being put out' tells you to rearrange RATE and EVIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative is a kinsman, someone connected to you by blood or marriage.

clue.text: Take a turn serving up drinks

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word for drinks is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nips are small drinks of spirits

explanation.surface: A bar worker takes a turn at the counter dishing out drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving up' reverses NIPS, which in a down entry reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to rotate or whirl round.

clue.text: Exercising iron rule which is catty

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a line is a ruled stroke, and a rule is a straight line

explanation.surface: Someone wielding power with an iron fist is being spiteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' and 'which is' only join the pieces to the definition; 'catty' is read literally as cat-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline means belonging to the cat family, which is the literal sense of cat-like.

clue.text: Drawing lines

parts.note: reads like sketching with a pen, but means cords used for hauling a vehicle along

explanation.definitionFit: Ropes used to pull a broken-down car or a barge are lines that draw, that is drag, something.

clue.text: Where people may enjoy themselves with legitimate reason

parts.note: fair means just or legitimate
a ground is a reason, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: A place of fun is justified by a sound argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair site is an open space with rides and stalls for public amusement.

clue.text: Get into gear

parts.note: reads like engaging a car's gearbox, but gear here is clothing, so it means to dress

explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone is to put garments, or gear, on them.

clue.text: Gather orchard produce is to be made available again

parts.note: to reap is to gather a crop
a pear is a fruit grown in orchards

explanation.surface: Harvesting the orchard brings fruit back into the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back into view or into supply after an absence.

clue.text: Going around dumping rubbish on a railway

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it, so it goes first

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone fly-tips rubbish onto a railway line while wandering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumping' only paints the scene; 'on' places ROT above A and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary describes something that revolves or turns round an axis.

clue.text: Love to meet, so it's said

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Arranging to meet a sweetheart, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Orally means by word of mouth, spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Very early bird has a point

parts.note: a daw is a jackdaw
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An early bird is given a sharp beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very early bird' is read as a whole, but the definition is just 'Very early', a noun used as an adverbial time.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the very start of the day, the earliest hour.

clue.text: Explains badly re-set print

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A printer's assistant reset the type badly and has to explain.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to clarify or make the meaning of something plain.

clue.text: Face a man of learning after six

indicators.note: the scholar comes after the number in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a sage is a wise or learned person

explanation.surface: Confronting a scholar after six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for the countenance.

clue.text: Giving a worker time to carry on is to arouse hostility

parts.note: a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker

indicators.note: the period of time holds the two short words inside it, carrying them

parts.note: an age is a period of time
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Letting an employee take time to keep going will make people angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' puts ON and IS inside AGE to make AGONISE. 'carry on' looks like one phrase, but its words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise is to provoke enmity or make someone an opponent.

clue.text: Note beer is provided for a journalist

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Beer is laid on for a newsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a newsgatherer who writes for a paper.

clue.text: Perfect country environment for conservationists

indicators.note: the country's name surrounds the other piece, forming its environment

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: A rural setting ideal for environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' means surroundings, so the country encloses the conservationists; NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic houses and land in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, complete and unbroken.

clue.text: Bread and ale together can be so easy to digest

indicators.note: the two words mixed together can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A simple meal of bread and beer goes down easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together can be' mixes BREAD and ALE into one new word; 'digest' means taking in written matter, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: Readable writing is easy to take in, and a digest is a summary for reading.

clue.text: Dicky, Sue, and Sam are to take over

indicators.note: dicky is slang for faulty or shaky, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Three people, one named Dicky, plan to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a person's name in a list, but it means unsound and rearranges SUE and SAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a role is to take it on, as in assume control.

clue.text: The French dream for retirement-something extra always

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: reve is the French word for a dream
more means an additional amount

explanation.surface: A French person dreams of retiring with a bit extra in the pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retirement' reverses REVE to give EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore means for all time, forever.

clue.text: Make good in the matter of business raised

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding
Co is the abbreviation for company
up means raised or lifted

explanation.surface: A matter of business is brought up for repayment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' is not a reversal signal here: it simply supplies UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover losses, making them good.

clue.text: The dress of thought" according to Samuel Johnson

definitions.text: The dress of thought" according to Samuel Johnson

parts.words: The dress of thought" according to Samuel Johnson
parts.note: Johnson wrote that this is the dress of thought: words clothe ideas

explanation.definitionFit: Words and speech are what ideas are clothed in when expressed.

clue.text: Men fighting a dreadful miser

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Soldiers set upon a horrible skinflint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges MISER into RMIES, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies are bodies of soldiers at war.

clue.text: A ship loaded with border plants

indicators.note: the ship carries the other piece as its cargo, inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A vessel is filled with herbaceous border plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border plants' reads as one gardening phrase, but 'border' is EDGE and only 'plants' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedges are grass-like plants of wet ground.

clue.text: Housing fit only for pigs went first as arranged

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen
led means went in front

explanation.surface: Pigs went first into their pen, as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Styled means designed or arranged in a particular fashion, as of hair.

clue.text: Men interrupting a woman with the right corrective

indicators.note: the men break into the woman's name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
taken as written
a Tory is a conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: Men barge into a woman's conversation while the right wing corrects her.
explanation.definitionFit: Amendatory means serving to amend, putting right a fault.

clue.text: Many a politician is rather wet!

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Plenty of politicians are feeble, the setter jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' in British slang also means feeble, which the surface plays on; here it means moist.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp means slightly moist, not fully soaked.

clue.text: Fine powder used in various industrial processes

indicators.note: the answer is put to use inside these words, sitting within one of them

explanation.surface: A technical note on a fine powder employed throughout manufacturing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a whole definition, but 'used in' signals letters lying inside 'industrial'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny dry particles of earth or matter make up a very fine powder.

clue.text: See law-breaker as a treacherous individual

indicators.note: something broken is smashed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal is seen as a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'law-breaker' looks like a criminal, but 'breaker' breaks up SEE and LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel, figuratively, is a sly, deceitful person.

clue.text: Legal claim certain to occasion amusement

parts.note: a plea is a claim made in court
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A lawsuit that is sure to win brings enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or delight.
